data.narrative:
Proteus Space is a Series A aerospace company founded by David Kervin (20+ years in US military government contracting) and Andrew Shapiro (20 years at NASA JPL, managed technology formulation including 3D-printed components for Mars Perseverance). The company has raised $14.4M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $17M total-raised proxy, yielding a $34M implied valuation. Peer-median triangulation is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector companies exist, fewer than three meet tight same-stage and valuation-tier criteria. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue data, though the Space & Aerospace median trades at 26.4x sales across the five public tickers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $29M to $39M, centered on $34M. This range reflects a single applicable method, introducing material uncertainty. Key unknowns include Proteus's revenue trajectory, customer concentration, and the timing of near-term contract wins—factors typical for Series A aerospace businesses but unquantified in available data. Peer comps remain sparse at this stage and valuation tier; broader sector multiples (26.4x P/S) may not translate meaningfully without revenue visibility.
